title: Ministry of Education (MOE)
program_type: Ministry/index-level entry spanning school, pre-university and undergraduate awards administered by MOE and the Public Service Commission
duration: MOE Pre-University Scholarship: 2 years. ASEAN Scholarship: 6 years from Secondary 1, 4 years from Secondary 3 and 2 years from Pre-university 1, renewed each year on school performance. MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award: the length of the undergraduate degree with a service bond of 4 years for local study, 5 years for a non-English speaking country and 6 years for an English speaking country, plus a concurrent 3-year PGDE bond. MOE-AU Scholarship: undergraduate study, then a PhD scholarship under START, then a 4 to 6 year bond as academic staff.
description: The Ministry of Education's awards and scholarships page presents Singapore's merit-based education awards, inviting visitors to learn about the different awards and scholarships available. It lists the Centennial Fund Award, Edusave awards and scholarships, Edusave scholarships for Independent Schools, the ITE Progression Award, the MOE Pre-University Scholarship, the MOE-AU Scholarship, programme-specific scholarships for pre-university and secondary schools, the Singapore-Industry Scholarship, special awards, the UPLIFT Scholarship and the ASEAN Scholarship.

duration: Milestone-driven: first draft of papers due 8 June 2027 and final draft due 8 September 2027, with a work-in-progress workshop in June or July 2027

title: Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship (AEF) Program
degree: Not a degree programme - professional fellowship for K-12 STEM educators
official_source: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science, Office of Workforce Development for Teachers and Scientists (WDTS), administered with the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE)
duration: Eleven months, mid-August through mid-July; the fellowship begins on the third Monday in August with the initial programme Orientation

title: Office of Science Graduate Student Research (SCGSR) Program
official_source: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science, Office of Workforce Development for Teachers and Scientists (WDTS), administered with Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE)
duration: 3 to 12 consecutive months of research at a DOE laboratory/facility, within a project period bounded by published earliest and latest start dates
description: SCGSR provides supplemental awards to thesis-based doctoral students to conduct part of their dissertation research at a DOE national laboratory or facility, in collaboration with a DOE laboratory scientist, in a DOE Office of Science priority research area. Awardees receive a monthly living stipend of up to $3,600 while at the host laboratory, plus up to $3,000 total for inbound and outbound transportation if the host laboratory is more than 50 miles from their home graduate institution.
